# A decision written with and, or and not gets one mutant per condition,
# forcing that condition true and false while the others keep reading the
# template's real data.
#
# Forcing every condition at once only ever produces the then branch or
# the else branch, which if-true and if-false already cover. Forcing one
# leaves a decision that is still a function of the data, so whether a
# test notices depends on the data it renders with -- which is what shows
# whether anything is coupled to that condition in particular.
#
# TestPage renders with Admin false and Owner true. Nothing renders with
# Admin true, so forcing .Admin either way leaves what the test sees
# unchanged and both mutants survive.
#
# .Banned is absorbed: {{or .Banned (and .Banned .Loud)}} is just .Banned,
# so .Loud cannot change the decision and is reported dead rather than run.

muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}{{if and .Admin .Owner}}A{{end}}{{if or .Banned (and .Banned .Loud)}}B{{end}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Admin  bool
	Owner  bool
	Banned bool
	Loud   bool
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Owner: true}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), ""; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
